text:
alex: FYI seeing a cluster spike of GPU Xid errors (multiple 701/702) on us-west-2-gpupool-*. 3 different hosts in ~2h, all ML jobs got preempted. leaving initial dmesg excerpts below.

maria: ugh. can you paste the exact dmesg lines and the node IDs? we should check if it's flaky cards vs PCI resets.

alex: nodes: gw-usw2-gpu-23, gw-usw2-gpu-47, gw-usw2-gpu-51. sample dmesg line: `GPU 0: Xid 79 detected: ECC error, channel 0`. full tail:```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (0002:17) 79, pid=12345, GPU=0000:65:00.0
[ 1234.567910] NVRM: GPU at 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.```

samir: can we rule out kernel noisy dmesg truncation? we had cases where ring buffer small + high lograte hides pre-fail traces. recommend temporarily bumping kernel log buffer and journal retention on suspect hosts and re-run repro.

ingrid: +1. we already ship logs via log-collector but the snippet length default is 2k lines — not enough for rapid flood. propose capture playbook: increase dmesg ring buffer, collect dmesg, journalctl -k, systemd-coredump info, and a 5s nvidia-smi polling snapshot.

dinesh: adding a compact capture one-liner for oncall to run before draining node:```
# run as root on affected host
echo 4000000 > /proc/sys/kernel/printk_ratelimit_burst || true
dmesg --level=err,crit,warn -T -l err,warn,crit --follow --time-format iso > /tmp/gpu-dmesg-$(date +%s).log &
journalctl -k -b --no-pager | grep -i -E "xid|ecc|gpu|nvrm|pcie" > /tmp/gpu-journal-$(date +%s).log
nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,uuid,name,temperature.gpu,perf_state,fan.speed,driver_version --format=csv > /tmp/gpu-snapshot-$(date +%s).csv
# also capture NVML debug if available
cat /proc/driver/nvidia/params 2>/dev/null > /tmp/nv-params-$(date +%s).txt || true
# tar and upload
tar -czf /tmp/gpu-collect-$(date +%s).tgz /tmp/gpu-* && curl -F file=@/tmp/gpu-collect-$(date +%s).tgz https://s3-upload.internal/reports || echo upload-failed```

maria: nice. two notes: 1) use --since on journalctl when possible to limit bulk, 2) add `journalctl -u kubelet -u docker --no-pager --since "-15m"` to correlate container-level OOMs. also tag upload with node+boot-id.

alex: infra-bot just created a collection ticket: https://tickets.internal/infra/INC-4219 (attached collector link). :thumbsup:

infra-bot: snapshot uploaded to s3://redwood-diagnostics/usw2/2140623456/gw-usw2-gpu-23/ (preserves boot-id, md5 checksums).

samir: for parsing heuristics: we should look for these anchor events in order to attribute: PCIe AER (Advanced Error Reporting) entries, `GPU has fallen off the bus`, repeated `Xid` codes with same GPU index, followed by thermal/clock throttles. we can score snippets with a simple rule: pcie/reset(3) + xid(5) + nv-reset(2) => high confidence.

ingrid: agree. can we add a quick awk pipeline that extracts events and prints context +/- 200 lines to help triage automatically?

dinesh: quick awk/gawk pipeline:```
# extract context around key tokens from combined dmesg+journal output
awk 'BEGIN{tok["Xid"]=1;tok["fallen off the bus"]=1;tok["AER"]="AER"} {for(k in tok) if(tolower($0)~tolower(k)) {for(i=NR-200;i<=NR+200;i++) if(i in buf) print buf[i]; print "---EVENT---";}} {buf[NR]=$0; if(NR>1000) delete buf[NR-1000]}' /tmp/combined-log.txt > /tmp/triage-snippets.txt```

maria: we should standardize field names for the collector metadata (node, gpu-index, boot-id, driver-version, kernel, timestamp) so SRE tools can auto-ingest. I'll open a tiny PR to add fields to the uploader.

alex: operational playbook for oncall when Xid bursts hit: 1) run the collect one-liner 2) cordon+drain node (evict GPU jobs) 3) repro with a single-tenant stress test (small looped CUDA job) while collecting `nvidia-smi --query-compute-apps` and dmesg 4) if reproducible mark for replacement; if not, re-enable and monitor.

samir: also track a per-GPU short-term error rate metric (xid_count/5m) with alert thresholds. we had wins by detecting rising trend and preemptively moving pods.

ingrid: can we add a short k8s taint cmd snippet to the playbook?```
kubectl taint nodes gw-usw2-gpu-23 gpu-failed=true:NoSchedule --overwrite
kubectl drain gw-usw2-gpu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force```

alex: perfect. i'll run the collection on gw-usw2-gpu-23 now and paste the triage-snippets after upload. thanks all. :rocket:
